newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-THORPE PUTS ENGLAND IN COMMAND VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-THORPE PUTS ENGLAND IN COMMAND VS NZ.

text.p: A superb batting display from Graham Thorpe put England firmly in command of the second cricket test against New Zealand at lunch on the third day on Saturday.
England were 282 for four wickets in reply to New Zealand's first innings of 124, with Thorpe on 85 and John Crawley on 33.
England's hopes of building an imposing first innings lead were temporarily jeopardised when they lost their fourth wicket 10 minutes after play began.

Resuming at 204 for three, England had added only nine runs when Nasser Hussain was out for 64, caught at first slip after driving at a turning delivery from debutant teenage spinner Daniel Vettori. It was Vettori's first test wicket.
But Crawley and Thorpe set about putting substance into the England innings.
Although slow progress was made in the first hour, with several near misses off Vettori and fellow spinner Dipak Patel, England established a 158-run lead by lunch.

Thorpe, who brought up his half century with a dashing cut for four off Patel in the second over of the day, was in dominant form. He treated the crowd to some delightful square drives to the fence off anything wide of off-stump.
Crawley also looked in good touch, once lofting Patel over the mid-wicket boundary for six.

The pick of the bowlers was Vettori, who at 18 years and 10 days is New Zealand's youngest ever test cricketer. With one for 61 off 25 overs, he extracted good spin out of the drying pitch and troubled the batsmen with his well flighted, accurate deliveries.
